paper_metadata.title: Effects of tantalum concentration on the microstructures and mechanical properties of tungsten-tantalum alloys

evidence.quote: Pure tungsten and tungsten-tantalum alloys with tantalum concentrations of 5, 10, 15 and 20 wt.% were fabricated by spark plasma sintering.

High energy ball milling (HEBM) process was operated at a speed of 380 rpm for 30 h and the weight ratio of ball to powder was 5:1.

The samples were sintered by spark plasma sintering (SPS) in vacuum under a pressure of 80 MPa, and the maximum temperature was 1800 ◦C with heating rate of 100 ◦C/min. The holding time was chosen to be 0 min in order to limit grain growth.
Fig. 1 shows the XRD patterns of milled powder and sintered compacts. Small peaks of Ta can be found besides W peaks in all of the milled powders.

Small peaks of Ta can be found besides W peaks in all of the milled powders. However, for sintered compacts, small peaks of Ta only appear in W-15Ta/W-20Ta and cannot be observed in W-5Ta/W-10Ta anymore.
